chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Qurashī al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Alī ibn ‘Uthmān, from ‘Abd al-Jabbār al-Nahāwandī, from Abī Sa‘īd, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah, and Yūnus ibn Ḍabyān, and Abī Salamah al-Sarrāj, and al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ‘Umar, all of them said: We heard Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) saying:

Verily, when Abū ‘Abdillāh, al-Ḥusayn ibn ‘Alī (peace be upon him), passed away, the seven heavens, the seven earths, and what is within them, and what is between them, and those that circulate around them, and Paradise, and Hell, and everything our Lord created, both that which is seen and that which is unseen, wept over him.
ai.seo_question: What did the heavens and earth do when Imam Husayn died?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the universal scope of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (a.s.) martyrdom, portraying it as a cosmic event that triggered the grief of all created beings, from the seven heavens to the unseen realms. In Shia scholarship, this narrative underscores the metaphysical centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt, illustrating how their suffering resonates throughout the entire hierarchy of existence, thereby validating the spiritual authority of the Imams as the axis of creation.
